business_problem: Raleigh needed to improve congestion management, mobility, and street safety as the city grew, but manual traffic counts and disconnected sensor repositories made it hard to visualize conditions, respond to incidents quickly, or plan infrastructure changes proactively.
solution_summary: Raleigh combined NVIDIA smart-city AI with its geospatial digital twin to create a real-time traffic and urban-operations platform. NVIDIA DeepStream, part of the NVIDIA Metropolis suite, performs video analytics for vehicle counts, trajectory tracking, and other traffic observations at key intersections. Those live signals are integrated with Esri ArcGIS on Microsoft Azure, which powers the city's digital twin and lets engineers visualize traffic, pedestrian, and bicycle flows inside a 3D map for scenario simulation and event planning. The city is also testing NVIDIA Blueprint for video search and summarization to automate incident understanding through vision-language agents that detect hazards and generate text descriptions under live video feeds. Together, these layers connect sensor data, geospatial context, and AI alerting so Raleigh can move from reactive operations to predictive, citywide traffic and safety management.
products_used: NVIDIA Blueprint for video search and summarization (VSS)

data_flow: Traffic video and sensor feeds are analyzed by DeepStream and related AI agents, the resulting vehicle and incident signals are pushed into Raleigh's ArcGIS digital twin on Azure, and planners and operators use the live 3D map to visualize congestion, simulate scenarios, and trigger faster operational responses.
business_outcome: Raleigh achieved 95 percent vehicle-detection accuracy, boosted a 2.5-person traffic-engineering team's analytical capacity by 4x, identified a path to save commuters an estimated $9.7 million annually, and built a scalable city platform that will expand with 1,000 more cameras and broader public-safety use cases.
metrics: $9.7 million annually in time and fuel costs
Additional 1,000 cameras planned over the next 12 to 24 months
architecture_clues: Raleigh uses a digital twin on ArcGIS and Azure as the central visualization layer for traffic intelligence.
DeepStream-generated vehicle counts and trajectories are merged with geospatial context rather than analyzed in isolation.
The city is extending the same platform to flood detection, parking utilization, asset conditions, and other civic domains.

Raleigh adopted NVIDIA DeepStream, part of the NVIDIA Metropolis suite of vision AI tools.
DeepStream achieving 95% accuracy in vehicle detection for turning movement counts.
